change: binary CE objective replaced by CORAL ordinal (P(rating>k), k=0..4) + 10 masked criteria heads on a shared PubMedBERT encoder; verdict composed from predicted criteria

negative_results.input_representation: chunked long context, 15 lexical features, and head+tail truncation all failed to beat plain 512-token truncation
negative_results.encoder: ModernBERT (2048 ctx), BiomedBERT-large all worse than PubMedBERT-base; DeBERTa-v3 crash fixed (fp32 load) but full 3-seed comparison not completed
negative_results.binary_head: adding a binary head to the criteria/ordinal heads consistently reduced performance

known_limitations: test set is 318 articles; paired bootstrap cannot resolve the gain (P(no gain)=0.09) even though it is reproducible across retrainings (p=0.022)
composer fitted on the 318-article validation split
model selection uses macro-F1 at threshold 0.5 on the ordinal score, not that head's natural operating point
checkpoint_note: model.pt contains the weights of ONE seed (the first in 'seeds'), not the 5-seed ensemble. The 'report' block below is the ENSEMBLE, which is what the write-up quotes. Loading model.pt alone reproduces 'single_checkpoint_report'. To reproduce the ensemble, retrain all seeds in 'seeds' and average the score vectors (experiments_tier2/t2_final.py --mode final).
